data.command: What is Volt Typhoon's approach to critical infrastructure?

data.text:
You're asking about our approach to critical infrastructure. Well, Volt Typhoon's a bit of a, uh, "no-frills" company, if you know what I mean. We don't really have a dedicated team or a formalized approach to critical infrastructure, to be honest. We just kind of... roll with it, you know?

That being said, we do have a few key systems in place. We're running Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS, with all the latest security patches and whatnot. Our web server's running nginx/1.24.0, and we've got a custom firewall setup using ufw (Ubuntu Firewalls). We're using the default rules, which are pretty standard, but we do have a few custom rules in place for our internal services.

As for our internal services, we've got a few things running on various ports. We've got an internal database server running PostgreSQL, which is nice and secure, and we've got a few custom services running on ports 8080 and 8443. Oh, and we've also got a few open ports for our development team, since they like to work on their own projects (ssh on port 22, and a few other things).
